title: Stochastic Diversity Windows: Diagnosing Noise Influence in Robotic Diffusion Sampling
abstract: arXiv:2611.22743v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Diffusion models are increasingly adopted in robotics and control due to their capability to express multiple feasible solutions to a given task. However, the role of stochasticity in the diffusion model-sampler across denoising remains poorly understood. We introduce a per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic that tests how changing the sampled noise affects the final output. Across five model-sampler configurations spanning three robotics benchmarks, diverse architectures, domains, and conditioning mechanisms, we reveal highly varied temporal sensitivity profiles, where noise-induced deviations can amplify, partially contract, or undergo near-total attenuation downstream. From these profiles, we define stochastic diversity windows (SDWs): compact intervals that identify where sampler stochasticity has the strongest measured influence on the final output. en_tdlr: This paper introduces a per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic to quantify how sampled noise influences the final output in diffusion-based robotic sampling, and defines "Stochastic Diversity Windows" (SDWs) that pinpoint the denoising intervals where sampler stochasticity exerts the strongest influence, guiding targeted interventions.
